(APPENDIX A.)
ANNUAL COMMUNICATION
OF THE
EXECUTIVE COUNCIL.
To THE Forty-Third Annual Convention of the Psi
Upsilon Fraternity.-
The Executive Council would respectfully present their an
nual communication.
It gives the Council great pleasure to congratulate the Con
vention upon the continued prosperity of the Fraternity.
The petition for a
Chapter of the Fraternity from Syracuse
University passed by the last Convention was
appointed by the
Chapters. The Council then approved the Gamma a commit
tee and delivered to them a Charter, and authorized them to
constitute and form a Chapter of the Fraternity at Syracuse
University, to be known as the Pi Chapter. The Pi Chapter
was
accordingly founded on the 8th day of June, 1875. The
Council are
happy to report that the new
Chapter is flourishing
as well as its best friends could desire.
The amendment to the Constitution passed by the last Con
vention was ratified by the Chapters, and has been duly incor
porated into our Constitution. The Council earnestly hope
that this amendment will have the intended effect, although it
has not as yet. From the Treasurei's report, hereto annexed, it
will be seen that there are many Chapters still in arrears. The

29
above amendment will we
hope, when fully understood by the
Chapters, remedy this evil.
The Council have to report that under the advice of able
Lawyers the plan to
incorporate the Fraternity has been aban
doned as
impracticable.
In accordance with the instructions of the last Convention,
the Council have considered an amendment to the Constitution
to protect the Fraternity against illegal or injurious action on
the part of Chapters, and report the following :
Sec. Art. If any Chapter shall report to the Exe
cutive Council in writing any Chapter as acting in a manner
likely to seriously injure the Fraternity, or as acting unconstitu
tionally, the Executive Council shall investigate the facts, and
if they shall determine that it is lor the best interests of the
Fraternity that such Chapter should be withdrawn, they shall
report the matter with all data to the other Chapters for their
consideration, and if three fourths of the other Chapters shall
approve of such action by a two thirds ('�) vote, the charter of
the reported Chapter shall be withdrawn'and the Chapter shall
cease to exist.
The Council also advise that S' c. Art of the Constitution
be amended so as to compel Chapters to report the result of
their votes within say two weeks to the Council.
'Last Autumn the Council appointed a committee to investigate,the Cornell trouble. The report of this committee has
been submitted to the Chapters and a
copy is hereto annexed.
The Council fully approved of the arrangement made by the
committee, and considered it honorable alike to the Fraternity
and to the Petitioners at Cornell University. The committee
rejiorted a hearty desire on the part of the men at Cornell to do
whai> ever was right and fair. They accepted the terms offered
to them and have kept faith in every particular. They have
indeed, don� more tliap was asked of them, These men now

30
come before you as Petitioners for a Charter to establish a
Chapter. The Council feel that such an opportunity to found
a Chapter on a firm and substantial basis should not be al
lowed to pass. The Petitioners are men whom we can thorough
ly trust to carry out our
principles and to be in every respect
an honor to the Fraternity.
The Council request the Convention to repeal General Reso
lutions, Nos. 20 and 21, passed by the last Convention. They
have been" practically set aside since the arrangement referred to
above was made.
The Council have been unable to commence work upon the
new
catalogue, as some
Chapters have not yet sent in their list
of names. The Chapters are
greatly to blame in thus delaying
the publication of the much needed catalogue.
There is a
strong de.-^ire in some portions of the Fraternity to
introduce a new and very decided change in the relations of
gradual es to the active life of the Fraternity, which the Coun
cil would advise the Convention to take into considerationThe graduates are at present so separated from the active mem
bers that they hear little or no Fraternity news and soon feel
that for them the Fraternity is a thing of the past. This senti
ment, unfortunately only too common among our
graduates,
can, perhaps, be changed by introducing a new feature into ou^"
life It is proposed to establish graduate Chapters. . There
have been many plans discussed and no doubt several will be
submitted to you. In order that they should succeed it will be
necessary to guard against undue interference with them on the
part of undergraduate Chapters, and also equally necessary to
prevent them from unduly influencing the active body of the
Fraternity. Hence it is advisable that they should be consti
tuted as a distinct order in the Fraternity. They should have
the power to make their own laws and of choosing their own
members. They should of course be prohibited from taking in
any person who has not been duly initiated by an active
Phaptej-,

31
There is another change the council think could be made with
benefit to our
legislation. It is always desirable to attract a
large number of graduates to our
Conventions, and this may
be done by allowing graduates present at Convention one vote
collectively, or one vote for every thirty or
forty present, but
never less than one vote. They would probably have good effect
in attracting graduates to our
meetings.
Attention is called to the report of the Secretary and Trea
surer. The present financial condition of the Fraternity is great
ly to be regretted.
The Council asked that a tax of thirty cents per capita be
levied upon the Fraternity for the expenses of the Council for
the ensuing year.
Mr. A. G. Higginson of the Phi was
expelled by that Chap
ter, April 22nd, 1876, for conduct unbecoming a gentleman and
a brother of the Fraternity.
The Council leave the affairs of the Fraternity in the hands
of the Convention, confident of their ability to legislate for the
best interests of all.
FRED. A. BROWN,
President Executive Council.
GEO. C. COFFIN,
